items.title: Bank Branch Costs Hinge More on Market Than Management, JLL Finds
items.description: National CRE News In Your Inbox. Sign up for Connect emails to stay informed with CRE stories that are 150 words or less. National + Weekender | November 19, 2026 By: Amy Wolff Sorter Bank Branch Costs Hinge More on Market Than Management, JLL Finds Erin Haglund, JLL In early 2026, a Wall Street Journal article said that bank branches were closing at a rapid rate, due to the continued rise of digital banking. Between 2019 and 2024, over 6,000 branches nationwide closed. However, U.S. banks opened more branches in the first half of 2026 than they closed, “reflecting the first sustained expansion since the financial crisis and a historic shift after more than a decade of post-crisis consolidation,” according to JLL’s just-released “The Cost of Running a Retail Bank Branch Network” report . “Digital banking has fundamentally changed how customers transact, but it hasn’t eliminated the need for personal interaction,” Erin Haglund, managing director, financial services at JLL , told Connect CRE. “In many ways, it has made the purpose of the physical branch more important and more specialized.” While this might be good news for customers who prefer their banking to be up close and personal rather than online, it can also mean higher operating costs for the banks in question. Location Determines Costs Many of the expenses boil down to a branch’s locale. “What stood out most was just how much of a branch’s operating cost is determined by the market itself, rather than the decisions a bank makes about managing its facilities,” Haglund said. The JLL report explained that across 12 U.S. markets, facilities operating cost per square foot is 2.6 times higher at the top than at the bottom. The expenses include repair and maintenance, cleaning, snow clearance and grounds maintenance, while excluding rent, pass-through charges from landlords and capital spending. Annual costs per square foot by market are: New York City: $24.35 Chicago: $15.18 New Jersey: $14.94 Long Island, NY: $14.83 Houston: $12.76 Dallas-Fort Worth: $12.24 Philadelphia: $12.12 Hartford, CT: $12.10 Seattle/Puget Sound: $11.40 Baltimore, MD: $10.50 Washington, DC metro: $10.36 Orange County, CA: $9.23 The gap results from wage levels, climate and building format versus portfolio management. “Banks have historically relied on national benchmarks, standardized contracts, and broad cost-reduction targets to drive efficiency,” Haglund said. “But our research reinforces that a lower-cost branch isn’t necessarily a better-managed branch, and a higher-cost branch isn’t necessarily inefficient.” Cost Negotiation: A Non-Starter The problem faced by branches and banks is that less than one-third of operating budgets can be divided into categories in which vendor negotiation can lead to lower prices. Here’s why: Landlords set service charges, which are the largest single line in the budget Maintenance costs are the result of vendor availability, rather than contracted rates For example, negotiating cleaning service costs doesn’t yield much in savings due to rising wages, benefit costs and turnover. The report said that interior cleaning costs 48% more in heavy-union markets than in right-to-work markets, while fire and life safety costs 83% more. Furthermore, a cleaning line that includes supplies, waste handling, pest control and exterior work averages $4.78 per square foot, compared with $3.19 for general interior cleaning alone. That’s roughly a 50% difference for the same physical work. Haglund said that focusing on structural market costs rather than operating costs can help. “That allows banks to focus resources where they can actually influence outcomes rather than chasing savings that may not be achievable,” she said. Another issue is the growing shortage of skilled trades professionals to maintain the physical branches. JLL research reported that approximately 2.1 million skilled trades positions could go unfilled by 2030. Banks compete for such workers with data centers, life sciences and advanced manufacturing, especially in Sun Belt metros where both are expanding. When equipment fails, and no technician is available, the cost goes beyond the repair bill. “From a financial perspective, labor shortages can increase emergency service premiums, extend repair timelines and drive higher costs for temporary solutions,” Haglund said. “Deferred maintenance can also accelerate equipment deterioration and create more significant capital expenditures down the road.” JLL recommended that banks secure technician capacity and response times before negotiating price. Haglund added that banks should pool maintenance demand across networks, so vendor partners could better plan staffing. Meanwhile, landlords should focus on coordinating building maintenance, replacing equipment before it wears out, and keeping an eye on building systems. “Ultimately, we need to shift from a reactive maintenance model to one that is more predictive, coordinated and focused on protecting operational continuity,” Haglund said. Then, There’s the Weather It’s no secret that climate change is impacting commercial real estate, including physical branches. Citing Climate Central, the JLL report said that billion-dollar weather disasters have struck the U.S. about every 16 days on average over the past decade, compared with every 82 days in the 1980s. A single regional event (think a hurricane or snowstorm) can impact every branch in a market at once. The bank that relies on a few vendors could find it needs them all at once. One solution is for bank branch budgets to incorporate expected weather-related variances. “The objective isn’t necessarily to avoid higher-risk markets; it’s to understand the exposure, evaluate the economics, and design the appropriate level of resilience into the network,” Haglund explained. items.title: Buy Well, Run Better: Why Apartment Operations Outlast the Purchase Price
items.description: National CRE News In Your Inbox. Sign up for Connect emails to stay informed with CRE stories that are 150 words or less. National + Weekender | November 19, 2026 By: Amy Wolff Sorter Buy Well, Run Better: Why Apartment Operations Outlast the Purchase Price Tyler Chesser, CF Capital Buying a perfect apartment in a high-demand market at a reasonable cost is an investor’s dream. But purchase is only part of the equation when it comes to successful apartment investments. Experts and operators told ApartmentBuildings.com that much of the lasting advantage of ownership comes after the deal closes. "Buying well is a one-time win," said Tyler Chesser, co-founder and managing partner of CF Capital . "Operating well compounds every month you own the asset." Holistic Planning Determining a building’s location, purchase price, and capital structure can be the key to a successful multifamily purchase. Deals need to make financial sense for an investor. But there’s a catch. "Buying a great asset for a low price is the way to acquire real estate,” Ballast Co-Founder and CEO Gregory MacDonald said. “The problem is that this is exceptionally hard to do on a consistent basis." Even owning the best building in a thriving submarket isn’t a guarantee it will appreciate. The competition in certain markets and submarkets is fierce. There is always a shinier, prettier apartment complex around the corner. Unless there is a shortage of supply, an owner will rarely have the newest or best property. Greg MacDonald, Ballast "There will be a better one under permit, coming out of the ground in 12 months, and it is simply going to be newer," observed Tim Bruss, managing director of asset management with Hamilton Zanze . Furthermore, while price and building quality are fixed at acquisition, “operations are the part an owner can improve every year, and the gains compound," said Peter Salvatore, junior managing director, FirstService Residential . "A lower purchase price can be erased by deferred maintenance, and a better property can underperform if it is poorly run." In fact, sophisticated operations help improve an apartment building’s economics every day after closing. Said MacDonald: "A good basis gives you a sizable advantage on day one. Superior operations is how you maintain that advantage and build on it." "Having the experience to know where to put resources to create those differentiators is what makes the difference,” Bruss added. By the Numbers: Operations Mathematics Cap rates and net operating income analyses support how operational sophistication can boost a multifamily property’s value. Chesser explained that an asset carrying a 6% cap rate means that each NOI dollar can translate into approximately $16.67 of value. Tim Bruss, Hamilton Zanze So, if a 250-unit property improves its retention by five points, that means 12 unit turns per year are saved, saving $4,000 per unit per turn. This translates to about $50,000 added to the NOI, which can mean a value increase of more than $800,000. "You didn't need the market to do anything for that," Chesser said. There’s more. Lenders and writers underwrite both owner-operators and buildings. Operationally sophisticated owners/operators aren’t tied to market movements when determining apartment hold, refinance or sale strategies. Said Chesser: “when your NOI is solid and well-documented, you choose when to sell or refinance. When it isn’t, the market chooses for you.” On the other hand, while operations can help boost property value, it’s not a cure for poor capital structures or overleveraging. "Buying or building at a good basis doesn't guarantee success, just as operating at a high level won't make up for bad underwriting," said Garrett Karam, chief investment officer of Embrey . At the same time, many operators understand how to raise money and buy, but might not have a clue about operations. This can be where the trouble starts. "After a cycle of declining net effective rents, those groups are struggling and playing defense,” explained Hamilton Zanze CEO Kurt Houtkooper . Keys for Owner/Operators Peter Salvatore, FirstService Residential The sources provided specific steps for owners interested in successfully operating their properties. Focus on Asset Management Whether owners have a vertically integrated organization or outsource operations to third-party managers, they need to understand in depth what’s going on. Chesser suggested implementing a weekly scorecard of 10 to 15 leading indicators per property, assigning an individual to each indicator, and reviewing the information each week. In addition, “tie management fees and on-site bonuses to the outcomes you care about like retention, collections and expense control, not just occupancy,” he added. Data Matters Salvatore recommended starting with the data for planning, establishing a baseline for key metrics, benchmarking them against comparable properties and reviewing them monthly with management partners. Additionally, “operate with actual operating data instead of assumptions,” he said. Rebid, Rebid and Rebid Again Chesser suggested that there’s no harm in regularly rebidding services including landscaping, insurance, trash, utilities and others. items.title: Highland Park UMC Pastor: 'Disappointing' News on HPMC TRO
items.description: Live Poll A Dallas County judge on Wednesday partially granted Highland Park Methodist Church’s request for a temporary restraining order over the use of the Highland Park United Methodist Church name and branding. Last week, Highland Park Methodist Church, formerly Highland Park United Methodist Church, asked a judge for a temporary restraining order to prevent the Horizon Texas Conference (which is suing Highland Park Methodist Church) from referring to the group of members who wish to remain United Methodists as Highland Park UMC or any variation of a “confusingly similar” nature. The latter now holds services at Prothro Great Hall , just a quick walk from their old sanctuary. The court appears to have at least partially ruled in Highland Park Methodist’s favor. In an email to members last night, Rev. Andy Lewis, the newly-installed senior minister of what now can’t be called Highland Park UMC, said that the church would now regroup, and it has been forced to temporarily take down its website. The order blocks the conference from using variations of Highland Park United Methodist Church, and from soliciting donations under those names and logos. It does not prevent the denomination from operating a congregation or gathering under a different name. “This news is disappointing, but I want you to hear from me that I remain undeterred in our mission to offer a United Methodist ministry and witness to the Highland Park community and beyond,” Lewis writes. “There is an unmistakable flame of faith and commitment that is burning in our congregation, and this temporary setback will not snuff it out.” Yesterday’s ruling was not on the merits of the case itself—that will come later. (Unless the TRO is extended, it ends at 4 p.m. on December 2, or whenever the matter is taken up by the court, whichever comes first.) The denomination’s General Council on Finance and Administration holds the federal trademark registration for the words “United Methodist,” which covers, among other uses, identifying membership in the church. The denomination has also registered the cross and flame logo. The Horizon Texas Conference argues that the denomination’s rules allow its use of the full Highland Park United Methodist Church name, especially since the other church voted to leave the denomination. Highland Park Methodist Church says it's confusing to donors. The conference’s lawsuit against Highland Park Methodist Church remains pending. You can follow the story further here . items.title: How a Family Nonprofit in Frisco Evolved Into a $30 Million Foundation
items.description: Live Poll Kevin Hail was 13 when his parents sat him and his 20-year-old brother down at the kitchen table with an announcement. It was 1991, and his mother, Janelle Hail, wanted to educate women on breast cancer and the importance of early detection. She had been diagnosed 11 years prior. “They said, ‘We’re starting a nonprofit,'” Kevin says. “We had no idea what that meant. They said, ‘We’re going to do this as a family.’” That nonprofit is now the National Breast Cancer Foundation . Kevin Hail has been CEO of the National Breast Cancer Foundation since 2025. Courtesy National Breast Cancer Foundation Kevin’s responsibilities started as a teenager, licking envelopes and working fundraisers and going to hospitals. Then, in the late 1990s, the foundation grew alongside the emergence of the internet, which allowed it to reach new donors and corporate partners. The foundation’s early website attracted companies such as Procter & Gamble and Dick’s Sporting Goods, which partnered with the foundation through cause-marketing campaigns. Those partnerships brought in more funding and allowed the organization to build a national presence through expanded programming and more employees. In 2005, as the foundation expanded, Kevin’s parents asked him to join the organization full time. He's worked for the foundation as chief operating officer, president, and now CEO, as of 2025. (He was previously working in finance.) “I remember saying, ‘There’s no way I can work with my family. I love you guys, but we’re going to kill each other,’” he says. “But [as it turned out], we got along great.” Today, the Frisco-based foundation has more than 60 employees and about 8,000 volunteers nationwide. According to recent federal filings, the National Breast Cancer Foundation generated about $29.9 million in revenue in the fiscal year ending June 2025 and recorded about $27.1 million in expenses. It had approximately $26.3 million in total assets at the end of the year. Kevin’s mother, Janelle, who's now 80, remains involved in an advisory role. When she launched the foundation, “she felt like there weren’t enough options, and there wasn’t really a community of women who were able to support each other and give each other advice and counsel,” Kevin says. Breast Cancer Awareness Month is the foundation's biggest fundraising month—Kevin estimates that the foundation raises about 70 percent of its annual revenue in October. A highlight for Kevin this year was the second annual Rollertown Open golf tournament, held here in North Texas, which raised about $95,000. “One of the reasons we love live events is there’s the fundraising component, but we get exposure to people who we normally wouldn’t get in front of,” Kevin says, adding that Texas Rangers and Dallas Cowboys “sports heroes” attended this year. The foundation’s year-round programming includes funding mammograms and diagnostic screenings for women who can’t afford them, connecting newly diagnosed patients with nurse navigators, hosting retreats for women with metastatic breast cancer, and organizing support groups. (In North Texas, more than 350 women participate in the in-person support groups.) The organization also distributes about 30,000 Hope Kits annually—which include gifts like socks, makeup, and tea—for women diagnosed with breast cancer. Of the more than 300,000 women diagnosed each year in the U.S., Kevin says the foundation is able to reach about 10 percent with the kits. Volunteers help pack "Hope Kits" to be sent across the country to women diagnosed with breast cancer. items.description: Mark Woodroof steps down as CEO of BHGRE Gary Greene, Matt Woodroof to assume role by Emily Marek November 18, 2026 Matt Woodroof (left) will take over as CEO of BHGRE Gary Greene as his father, owner and former CEO Mark Woodroof, transitions to a chairman role. Mark Woodroof , owner and longtime CEO of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate Gary Greene , is transitioning from the chief leadership position to a chairman role. His son, Matt Woodroof, will assume the CEO position. Mark joined BHGRE Gary Greene in 1996 and purchased the company with his business partners in 2000. He became the sole owner in 2021. Previously Gary Greene’s chief operating officer, Matt joined the brokerage in 2009 and has held roles including special projects consultant, REO division director, director of operations and corporate partnerships and relocation director. He was promoted to vice president of strategy and innovation in 2019 and took over as COO in 2023. “Matt has a strong understanding of this company, our business and the people who make it successful,” Mark said in a press release. “I have tremendous confidence in his leadership and judgment. We have built a strong organization with people I deeply value, and knowing the company is in capable hands is important as I transition into my new role as chairman. Matt is the right person to lead Gary Greene into its next chapter. As chairman, Mark will maintain an active role in the business, with a focus on long-term strategy, guidance and support. Matt, meanwhile, will take over day-to-day operations. “I’m looking forward to leading Gary Greene alongside an experienced and dedicated team,” said Matt. “Our focus is on building a brokerage where agents have the expertise, resources and strategic support to build exceptional businesses, and where consumers can expect an equally exceptional real estate experience. items.title: Parkland Communities secures $50M development financing, begins Highland Brook in Dacula
items.description: Parkland Communities secures $50M development financing, begins Highland Brook in Dacula by John Yellig November 18, 2026 The financing was seeded with a $15 million loan to fund Highland Brook. Via Parkland Communities. Parkland Communities recently secured a $50 million borrowing-base production facility with Anchor Loans to grow its homebuilding operations, starting with its 103-home Highland Brook community in Dacula. The financing is solely dedicated to Parkland Communities' for-sale housing operations and was seeded with a $15 million loan to fund Highland Brook. The facility provides capital for developed lots, entitled land and development costs, as well as new home construction. Parkland said it will pursue residential land and developed lots across Georgia. "Periods of uncertainty create some of the best opportunities for companies that are prepared to act," Parkland President Jim Jacobi said. "While others may be pulling back, we're focused on growth. Our relationship with Anchor Loans gives us the ability to be selective, act fast and pursue the right land opportunities to bring new communities to market. items.title: Thanksgiving Costs at Home Jump 6% in 2026 as Grocery and Utility Bills Hit Hosts Hard
items.description: Thanksgiving is the perfect time for loved ones to gather over a delicious, hearty meal. But in 2026, that feast could come with a higher price tag than we’d like. According to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person . That’s because staples like turkey, milk, rolls, and cranberries have shot up in price. And unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store. You may also notice a spike in your utility bills as your home’s systems are forced to work harder to keep everyone comfortable. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) found that the average family already uses over 300 gallons of water per day at home . With increased usage from additional showers, dishwashing, and hand-washing that are typical during the holidays, costs are sure to climb. “Having guests over greatly drives up money spent on groceries, but it also drives up utility costs. Preparing all of that food often involves keeping ovens and burners running for multiple hours and using large amounts of water in both the cooking and cleaning processes,” explains Carrie Bernard , founder and recipe developer at Eating on a Dime . Fortunately, it’s still possible to enjoy Thanksgiving without breaking the bank. A bit of planning and creativity can help keep your grocery expenses and utility bill in check. Loading... Americans cooking a Thanksgiving dinner will face higher prices overall this year, with the cost of the average 10-person dinner increasing by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person. American Farm Bureau Federation Why do costs vary by location? Where you live can also impact how much you spend this Thanksgiving. The American Farm Bureau found that the 10-person classic dinner in the Northeast is about 5% higher than the national average of $61.57. Costs in the West ($58.74) and Midwest ($56.89) are closer to the national average. And if you live in the South, you could expect to pay around $54.33. There are a few reasons for these cost differences. “They largely have to do with supply chains, since different regions require different imports, and these imprints cost more the further they travel,” says Bernard. Since the Northeast is generally colder, it relies more heavily on imports for many Thanksgiving staples, which leads to a higher cost for consumers. Also, the Northeast typically has higher operating costs for businesses, meaning that grocery prices are often higher. “However, prices vary widely between different stores, and many of them offer special holiday promotions, so there are usually savings to be found,” Bernard adds. Loading... The American Farm Bureau Federation puts a 16-pound turkey at an average of $23.68 (~$1.48/lb) in 2026. Tada Images - stock.adobe.com How to trim grocery and energy expenses While grocery and energy costs may be higher this Thanksgiving, these tips can help reduce them and enjoy the holiday without overspending. Look for grocery promos Jim Wang , founder at Wallet Hacks in Fulton, MD , suggests exploring promotions at your local supermarkets and groceries. “Many stores know consumers are being squeezed and often try to put out promos around Thanksgiving. They may offer the turkey at a low cost to get you to make your entire holiday purchase there,” Wang explains. Consider a potluck style meal Depending on how you celebrate Thanksgiving and who attends your meal, a potluck might make sense. “Every year, we do a potluck with friends and everyone brings something to share. This defrays the costs across everyone and while you don't end up with nearly as many leftovers, that's also excess spending you can avoid, especially if Thanksgiving leftovers don't excite you,” says Wang. Be conservative If you’re hosting, be a bit more conservative about how much everyone will eat. “Sometimes we get concerned about having guests leave hungry and we make too much as a result,” Wang says. It’s perfectly OK to make less of the more expensive items, like proteins, and bigger portions of sides that they can fill up on. Chances are your guests may prefer those sides to the turkey anyway. Use your air fryer and slow cooker Bernard tries to use her air fryer and slow cooker rather than my full oven when possible. “These appliances are highly versatile and able to cook a wide variety of dishes, and they consume much less energy in the process,” explains Bernard. Unlike ovens, which leak out heat and consume more energy the more you open the door to check on your food, air fryers and slow cookers cook things quickly and efficiently with low energy. “I try to only use the oven when it’s required due to the size or amount of food involved,” Bernard adds. items.title: Broker Action Coalition pushes for QM change on compensation cap
items.description: The Broker Action Coalition (BAC) is proposing a change to federal mortgage rules that would exclude lender-paid mortgage broker compensation from the Qualified Mortgage (QM) points-and-fees calculation, aligning its treatment with compensation paid to retail lenders' employee loan officers. In a white paper recently released by BAC , the coalition argues that the current rules create an uneven playing field between independent mortgage brokers and retail lenders, particularly on smaller-balance loans . Under the Ability-to-Repay/Qualified Mortgage rule, points and fees generally cannot exceed 3% of a loan amount for loans of $137,958 or more in 2026. Smaller loans are subject to graduated percentage and dollar limits. Currently, compensation paid by a wholesale lender to an independent mortgage broker counts toward that limit, while compensation paid by a retail lender to its own employee loan officer is excluded. The coalition argues that both types of compensation are often funded through the interest rate and are indistinguishable from the borrower's perspective. The difference can leave brokers with less room to cover other fees that count toward the cap, potentially causing otherwise qualifying loans to exceed the limit while losing QM status and its associated liability protections. The disparity is particularly pronounced on smaller loans, where the dollar limits leave less room for additional charges. The coalition said small-balance and rural loans are particularly vulnerable because fixed-dollar charges consume a larger share of the available cap. Small-dollar lending hurdles The white paper also points to a decline in small-dollar mortgage lending. The share of home purchase loans under $70,000 fell from more than 11% in 2011 to less than 4% in 2020, citing research from Pew Charitable Trusts , the Urban Institute and the Department of Housing and Urban Development . In rural and lower-cost markets, the group argues, the restrictions can make it harder for brokers to compete for loans that are already less financially attractive to originate. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau 's 2013 rulemaking established the distinction between employee and broker compensation. At the time, the bureau said including broker compensation in the calculation could help reduce the risk of mortgage brokers steering borrowers toward more expensive transactions. The coalition acknowledges that consumer protection concern but argues that subsequent regulations addressing loan originator compensation and steering have made the points-and-fees restriction a less targeted way to address the issue. Specifically, the group points to existing rules that prohibit loan originator compensation from varying based on a loan's interest rate or other terms, as well as a separate prohibition on steering borrowers toward transactions that provide greater compensation. The proposed reform would take two approaches: The primary proposal is a statutory amendment to the Truth in Lending Act that would exclude rate-funded creditor-to-broker compensation from the points-and-fees definition when it is paid under a compliant loan originator compensation agreement. The parallel regulatory proposal would ask the CFPB to amend Regulation Z to create the same exclusion. "The proposed reform would remove an inequitable regulatory constraint without changing the competitive forces that influence compensation today," the paper reads. "While individual brokerages may adjust their compensation arrangements, there is little evidence to suggest that the reform would materially diminish the wholesale channel 's overall pricing competitiveness." Avoiding circumvention Under the proposed language, the exclusion would apply only when compensation is funded through the interest rate, is not paid directly by the borrower or financed into the loan amount, and is established through a standing agreement between the creditor and broker that does not vary based on individual loan terms. The coalition said the proposed requirements would prevent brokers from adjusting compensation on individual loans to circumvent the cap. The change would leave the 3% limit and existing compensation and anti-steering rules intact, with borrower-paid compensation and other fees still subject to the cap. Data from two wholesale lenders representing $13.4 billion in combined 2026 production showed that loans with 2.75% broker compensation accounted for 14.53% of units and 12.41% of volume. BAC said the figures indicate most brokered loans close with lower compensation. The group also argued that the CFPB has authority under the Truth in Lending Act to make the change to preserve access to affordable mortgage credit. It cited the bureau's 2019 assessment of the Ability-to-Repay and Qualified Mortgage rule, which documented fee waivers and other challenges affecting smaller brokered loans. recent_coverage.summary_zh: ARCTRUST 与 Edison Equity 在奥斯汀西南部启动 Serenova 长者社区建设。项目共 175 套住宅，面向 55 岁及以上住户，计划于 2028 年秋季完工。

recent_coverage.title: FASB rule could push community banks to sell servicing
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 National Mortgage News 报道，美国财务会计准则委员会拟议的会计标准可能使部分金融机构更难评估按揭服务权价值，社区银行或因此出售相关服务权。

recent_coverage.title: Single-Family Permitting Weakens While Multifamily Activity Remains Stronger
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 数据显示，2026 年截至 September 的年初至今，美国独栋住宅许可为 689,884 套，同比下降 3.0%；多户许可为 393,778 套，同比增长 4.1%。

recent_coverage.title: Hedge fund pressures Invitation Homes to speed up home sales
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Land & Buildings 敦促 Invitation Homes 加快售房、增加资本返还并收缩增长计划。该投资者认为公司股价显著低于住宅价值，其估值判断尚非已实现交易结果。

recent_coverage.title: Where Developers Are Trying To Lease Public Lands To Build Data Centers
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Bisnow 核查发现，美国联邦机构正考虑出租至少 17 块公共土地，合计 19,200 英亩，用于数据中心及电力基础设施；相关项目处于已获批或待授权阶段。

recent_coverage.title: Service Properties Trust Rejects $2B Cash Bid, Claims Hotel Portfolio Could Be Worth Double
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Service Properties Trust 拒绝 20 亿美元酒店资产报价，计划保留 77 家酒店至明年起出售。董事会寄望盈利改善抬升售价，但第三季度净亏损扩大、每股运营资金下降。

recent_coverage.title: Who Owns Outright? Mortgage Status, Lock-In and Senior Homeownership
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 研究显示，2025 年美国自住房中 41% 无按揭；75 岁及以上业主的无按揭比例则较 2010 年下降。研究认为，低息贷款锁定效应可能影响代际住房交接时点。

recent_coverage.title: Blackstone's Data Center REIT Makes First Investment With $5B AWS Deal
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 黑石旗下 BXDC 拟收购两家 AWS 合资企业的 75% 股权，交易估值 50 亿美元。组合由亚马逊全额回租，初始三净租期 12 年，租金获 AWS 担保，预计年底前交割。

recent_coverage.title: Lenders increasingly pull with new credit score model, but few use it for pricing
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美国银行研究显示，调用 VantageScore 4.0 的贷款机构增多，但多数仍以 Classic FICO 定价；10 月新模型定价约占常规发行量的 8%，采用主要集中于 Rocket 和 UWM。

recent_coverage.title: Fed warns of financial risks from AI-driven market optimism
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美联储在周五的半年度金融稳定报告中再次将资产高估值列为主要风险，并指出数据中心开发企业、信贷市场、私人贷款人与特殊目的融资工具的复杂关联需密切监测。

recent_coverage.title: IPA Arranges $40.3M in Financing for North San Antonio Apartment Community
recent_coverage.summary_zh: IPA 为圣安东尼奥北部 Birwood Heights 公寓安排 4,030 万美元融资。该项目建于 2019 年，共 312 套住宅，贷款期限为 3 年，采用无追索权结构。

recent_coverage.title: Nearly Two-Thirds of Phoenix-Area Residents Have Considered Moving Because of Housing Costs, New Survey Finds
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NRHC 公布的凤凰城地区调查显示，65% 受访居民曾因住房成本考虑搬迁，租户中该比例为 77%；55% 支持增建出租住宅，反映可负担性压力与新增住房支持并存。

recent_coverage.title: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 纽约联储数据显示，第三季度信用卡余额增至创纪录的 1.29 万亿美元，同比增长 4.2%。报道援引贷款业人士指出，高消费债务对储蓄较少、财务空间较紧的首次购房者影响更大。

recent_coverage.title: Stream Realty Partners Brokers Sale of 2.7 MSF Industrial Park in Northwest Houston
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Adkisson Group 与 PCCP 合资企业收购休斯敦西北部 Northwoods 工业园，面积 270 万平方英尺，成交时出租率为 98%；IPA 同时安排收购融资及合资结构。

recent_coverage.title: The Tuccori commission settlements were supposed to wrap up, then the judge asked for more
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Tuccori 购房佣金诉讼和解尚未获最终批准。法院要求补充说明和解金额的确定方式、公平性、被告支付能力及继续诉讼的潜在回收额，相关主体的诉讼不确定性延续。

recent_coverage.title: Shorenstein Acquires 300,000 SF Office Tower in North Dallas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Shorenstein 收购达拉斯北部 30 万平方英尺的 Sherry Lane Place 办公楼。项目近期已升级会议及租户设施，买方计划继续改造大堂、户外座席并增设配套。

recent_coverage.title: Why analysts have a less rosy outlook for banks in 2027
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美国货币监理署在半年度风险报告中警示人工智能热潮相关风险，指出数据中心融资采用的新型金融和合同结构，在压力环境下的表现记录有限。

recent_coverage.title: Amid ‘economic headwinds,’ Boston looks to ease its inclusionary zoning policy
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 波士顿市长提议降低开发商代缴费用、延长可负担住房付款安排，并暂将多户住宅适用门槛由 7 套提高至 10 套。市府称方案旨在降低前期成本、改善开发可行性。

recent_coverage.title: Waterfall Originates Loan for Disneyland Lodging Property
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Waterfall 向 Dynamic City Capital 提供 4,800 万美元优先抵押贷款，为阿纳海姆 Portofino 酒店再融资。资金将用于偿还原贷款及改造，该酒店拥有 190 间客房。

recent_coverage.title: Realpage’s New York lawsuit tests the limits of algorithmic rent-pricing bans
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 挑战纽约州住宅租金算法禁令的诉讼持续。法律专家认为，案件可能厘清地方监管此类技术与商业言论保护之间的界限，但最终裁决的影响仍难估计。

recent_coverage.title: Craig Hall Is Betting on the Future of Office. His Next Chapter at HALL Park Is Taking Shape.
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HALL Group 正推进弗里斯科 HALL Park 下一阶段，包括甲级办公楼、公园扩建及住宅开发。项目近期获得摩根大通承诺入驻及 Public Storage 总部迁入，租赁动能回升。

recent_coverage.title: Realpage Economy Express Episode 75
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 援引劳工统计局数据称，10 月新增就业 165,000 人，失业率降至 4.1%；同期消费者价格环比涨 0.4%。成屋销售降至 2010 年以来最慢水平。

recent_coverage.title: Renewals Carry Apartment REIT Pricing as Coastal and Sun Belt Results Split
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 指出，2026 年第 3 季度续租与低流失率支撑公寓 REIT 定价，但阳光带多地新租约承压；沿海布局较重的运营商上调指引，阳光带同业下调预期。

recent_coverage.title: Legislative risk continues to cloud BTR’s capital outlook; here's why
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 尽管 BTR 获得机构投资者禁令豁免，实施规则及潜在新法仍压制资本投入。全国公寓协会数据显示，2026 年第 3 季度 BTR 在建量同比降 18.5%，社区销售额降 51.5%。

recent_coverage.title: Rising rents draw Wall Street money to industrial outdoor storage lot investments across the U.S.
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 Newmark 与 Alterra 数据，2020 年至今年第 3 季度，8 个主要市场工业露天堆场平均租金上涨 103.5%，每可用英亩月租近 11,000 美元，但南佛罗里达与萨凡纳涨幅落后传统工业物业。

recent_coverage.title: Building Material Price Inflation Remains High Despite Energy Price Declines
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 报告显示，10 月新建住宅投入价格环比涨 0.3%、同比涨 10.4%；能源投入价格环比降 3.3%，但建材价格仍环比涨 0.5%、同比涨 5.8%。

recent_coverage.title: SpaceX Unveils $74B Data Center Plans In Texas, Arizona
recent_coverage.summary_zh: SpaceX 宣布在亚利桑那州和得克萨斯州分别规划 500 亿和 240 亿美元数据中心项目；得州项目拟自建燃气电厂，亚利桑那项目将至少部分使用当地合作社电力。

recent_coverage.title: No Relief: Credit Conditions for Builders Still Tightening
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 调查显示，2026 年第 3 季度住宅土地收购、开发与建设贷款净宽松指数为 -15.3，连续 19 个季度收紧；各类贷款成本季度变化较小，方向不一。

recent_coverage.title: Apartment rents diverge: San Francisco rises, the Sun Belt falls
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 数据显示，10 月全国同店要价租金同比涨 1.7%，环比降 0.7%；该机构称同比改善主要来自比较基数。旧金山同比涨 14.7%，圣安东尼奥降 2.6%。

recent_coverage.title: Members Of Congress Have Questions For Brookfield After Its Mass Mobile Home Purchase
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Brookfield 第 2 季度从 GIC 收购 Yes Communities，后者运营逾 55,000 个住宅地块。3 名众议员要求其就租户保护作出保证，回复期限为 11 月 20 日。

recent_coverage.title: Compass sues 15 MLSes over listing policies
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Compass 在 8 个州分别对 15 家多重上市服务机构提起联邦反垄断诉讼，争议涉及经纪人在 MLS 之外营销部分房源可能遭罚款的挂牌规则。

recent_coverage.title: Rapid absorption continues even as deliveries slow for the Phoenix multifamily market
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，2026 年第 3 季度凤凰城公寓净吸纳逾 5,500 套，交付放缓推动运营改善；稳定运营物业空置率为 6.5%，月租 1,524 美元，但销售活动放缓。

recent_coverage.title: Tucson multifamily rents push higher as vacancy tightens
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 报告显示，2026 年第 3 季度图森公寓空置率降至 7.2%，同比下降 160 个基点；平均月租季度上涨 1.2% 至 1,163 美元，年内各季度租金均有增长。

recent_coverage.title: Raleigh-Durham multifamily vacancy tightens as deliveries slow
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，2026 年第 3 季度罗利--达勒姆公寓空置率降至 7.4%；年内交付近 4,400 套，同比降 54%。月租季度降 0.4% 至 1,585 美元，同比仍涨 0.9%。

recent_coverage.title: New, pending, closed listings remain depressed in Houston
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 休斯敦地产经纪人协会数据显示，截至 11 月 9 日当周，新挂牌 3,146 套，同比降 7%；住宅签约 1,402 套，同比降 29.5%，成交 1,275 套，同比降 17%。

recent_coverage.title: MarketBeat Raleigh-Durham Life Sciences Q3 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 高纬环球报告显示，2026 年第 3 季度罗利--达勒姆生命科学物业净吸纳连续第 4 个季度为正；空置率环比升至 26.4%，仍低于上年同期的 28.0%。

recent_coverage.title: CenterCal makes Arizona debut with $117M retail acquisition in tight market
recent_coverage.summary_zh: CenterCal 以 1.167 亿美元收购凤凰城郊区皮奥里亚的 Park West 购物中心，首次进入亚利桑那州。该项目占地 45 英亩，交易发生于凤凰城零售空置率下降之际。

recent_coverage.title: October 2026 Hottest Housing Markets
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 的 2026 年 10 月榜单显示，哈特福德居首，前 20 名连续第 37 个月仅来自东北与中西部；热门市场每套房源浏览量为全国均值的 2.6 倍。

recent_coverage.title: Oppenheimer & Co. Signs 220,000 SF Office Headquarters Lease in Lower Manhattan
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Oppenheimer 已在 RXR 持有的曼哈顿下城 32 Old Slip 签署约 220,000 平方英尺总部租约，覆盖 6 层，预计于 2028 年第 1 季度入驻。

recent_coverage.title: The seasonal decline in housing inventory is in full force
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HousingWire 数据显示，11 月 6 日至 13 日在售库存从 902,740 套降至 895,988 套，同比仍增 7.11%；该媒体指出，利率上行冲击需求，新挂牌近期变化不大。

recent_coverage.title: How Training Veterans in Skilled Trades Could Speed Up Homebuilding and Ease Housing Costs
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HBI 研究称，技工短缺使每套住宅建造时间延长近 2 个月，并导致 2024 年少建 19,000 套住宅。该机构认为，培训退伍军人及转业军人可成为补充劳动力的途径。
